classes.intro: The historical A–E classes split the IPv4 address space before CIDR arrived: each wedge's area shows its share of the whole. Click a class for the details.
classes.note: Each wedge's area is its share of the full IPv4 address space.
classes.use.A: The largest blocks: historically handed to ISPs, universities and very large organisations (Apple, IBM, the U.S. military).
classes.use.B: Mid-size blocks for universities, hospitals and mid-to-large businesses.
classes.use.C: Small blocks for home and small-business LANs — the range most home routers hand out from.
classes.use.D: Reserved for multicasting: one sender, many receivers (streaming, video conferencing). Never split into public/private.
classes.use.E: Reserved for research and future use, not allocated for public or private use.
